properties.name: Moscou / Moscow (Russia)
properties.description: Napoleon officially abandons a burning Moscow, giving the signal for 100,000 troops and thousands of civilian wagons to begin the march westward.

properties.name: Malo-Jarosewli / Maloyaroslávets (Russia)
properties.description: The Blocked Escape Route. A fierce battle breaks out as the French attempt to break through to a southern, untouched retreat route. Though tactically a draw, the engagement forces Napoleon to turn his army back onto the devastated, food-depleted northern road they used during the initial invasion.

properties.name: Mozhaisk / Borodinó
properties.description: Revisiting the Graveyard. The retreating army passes back through the Borodino battlefield, where tens of thousands of unburied, decomposing corpses from the bloody September battle still litter the landscape, severely damaging French morale.

properties.name: Wizma / Viazma (Russia)
properties.description: The First Winter Strikes. Russian forces attack the overextended French rear guard. Shortly after this battle, the first severe winter snows arrive, causing massive casualties among the ill-equipped French troops.

properties.name: Smolensk / Smolensk (Russia)
properties.description: Event: The Collapse of Discipline. The army arrives expecting massive stockpiles of food, only to find the depots depleted or rapidly looted by frantic advance units. The loss of order turns the organized retreat into a desperate survival scramble.

properties.name: Krasny / Krasnyi (Russia)
properties.description: Marshal Ney’s Rear Guard Action. Surrounded by Russian forces, Napoleon uses his Imperial Guard to keep the main escape path open. Marshal Michel Ney fights a legendary, desperate action to break through the encirclement with the rear guard.

properties.name: Orscha / Orsha (Belarus)
properties.description: The Imperial Regroup. Napoleon attempts to reorganize the remaining forces and re-establish military order. He is forced to abandon a massive portion of the army's remaining artillery pieces due to the deaths of thousands of horses.

properties.name: Studienska / Studenka (Belarus)
properties.description: The Berezina River Catastrophe. French engineers build temporary bridges over the freezing river. Amid chaotic Russian artillery fire, thousands of soldiers and civilian stragglers drown, freeze, or are left behind when the bridges are burned to stop the pursuing Russians.

properties.name: Smorgoni / Smorgon (Belarus)
properties.description: Napoleon Departs. Recognizing the political instability in France and the total loss of his army, Napoleon leaves his troops in disguise, handing operational command over to Murat as he rushes back to Paris to secure his throne.

properties.name: Vilna (Vilnius)
properties.description: Las tropas exhaustas y enfermas entran a territorio lituano.

properties.name: Kowno / Kaunas (Latvia)
properties.description: Crossing the Niemen. The broken remnants of the army re-cross the Niemen River, finally exiting Russian territory. Marshal Ney is famously reported to be the last French soldier to cross the bridge, marking the definitive, tragic end of the campaign.

properties.name: Tarantino / Tarutino (Russia)
properties.description: Battle of Vinkovo). Russian forces under General Bennigsen launched a surprise attack against Marshal Joachim Murat’s vanguard. While Murat managed to escape, this defeat served as the final catalyst that convinced Napoleon he could no longer maintain his position, prompting the grand evacuation of Moscow the very next day (October 19).

properties.name: Molodezno / Maladzyechna (Balrus)
properties.description: The 29th Bulletin. Napoleon halts here to draft a shocking official message to Paris, admitting for the first time that the army has suffered an unprecedented disaster, famously concluding with: "The health of His Majesty has never been better."

properties.name: Botr / Bobr (Belarus)
properties.description: Burning the Baggage. Reaching Bobr, Napoleon establishes a temporary headquarters. He orders the burning of the state archives, secret papers, and luxury imperial baggage to free up wagons and horses for the wounded.
